hints: Convert the given percentages into standard normal cumulative probabilities: $\mathrm{P}(X < 8.8) = 0.75$ and $\mathrm{P}(X < 7.7) = 0.175$.
Use standard normal tables to find the corresponding $z$-scores: $z_1 = 0.674$ for the upper tail, and $z_2 = -0.935$ for the lower tail using symmetry $\Phi(-z) = 1 - \Phi(z)$.
Form two linear equations in $\mu$ and $\sigma$ using $z = \dfrac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$, eliminate $\mu$ to solve for $\sigma$, then back-substitute to find $\mu$.
walkthrough:
Standardize the upper tail condition $25\%$ longer than $8.8$ cm:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 8.8) = 0.25 \implies \mathrm{P}(X < 8.8) = 0.75$$
$$\Phi(z_1) = 0.75 \implies z_1 = 0.674$$
$$\frac{8.8 - \mu}{\sigma} = 0.674 \implies \mu + 0.674\sigma = 8.8 \quad \text{--- (1)}$$

Standardize the lower tail condition $17.5\%$ shorter than $7.7$ cm:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 7.7) = 0.175$$
Since this probability is less than $0.5$, $z_2$ is negative:
$$1 - \Phi(-z_2) = 0.175 \implies \Phi(-z_2) = 0.825 \implies -z_2 = 0.935 \implies z_2 = -0.935$$
$$\frac{7.7 - \mu}{\sigma} = -0.935 \implies \mu - 0.935\sigma = 7.7 \quad \text{--- (2)}$$

Solve the simultaneous equations for $\mu$ and $\sigma$:
Subtract equation (2) from equation (1):
$$(0.674 - (-0.935))\sigma = 8.8 - 7.7$$
$$1.609\sigma = 1.1 \implies \sigma = \frac{1.1}{1.609} \approx 0.6837 \approx 0.684$$
Substitute $\sigma$ back into equation (1):
$$\mu = 8.8 - 0.674(0.68365) = 8.8 - 0.4608 = 8.3392 \approx 8.34$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Set up the first standardization equation from the upper tail data.
$25\%$ of women have finger lengths exceeding $8.8$ cm:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 8.8) = 0.25 \implies \mathrm{P}(X < 8.8) = 1 - 0.25 = 0.75$$
Look up $0.75$ in the standard normal cumulative distribution table:
$$\Phi(0.674) \approx 0.7498, \quad \Phi(0.675) \approx 0.7502 \implies z = 0.674$$
Apply the standardization formula $Z = \dfrac{X - \mu}{\sigma}$:
$$\frac{8.8 - \mu}{\sigma} = 0.674$$
Multiply both sides by $\sigma$ and rearrange:
$$8.8 - \mu = 0.674\sigma \implies \mu + 0.674\sigma = 8.8 \quad \text{[Equation 1]}$$

Set up the second standardization equation from the lower tail data.
$17.5\%$ of women have finger lengths shorter than $7.7$ cm:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 7.7) = 0.175$$
Because the area is less than $0.5$, the $z$-score is negative ($z < 0$).
Use the symmetry property $\Phi(z) = 1 - \Phi(-z)$:
$$1 - \Phi(-z) = 0.175 \implies \Phi(-z) = 1 - 0.175 = 0.825$$
Look up $0.825$ in the standard normal table:
$$\Phi(0.935) \approx 0.8251 \implies -z = 0.935 \implies z = -0.935$$
Substitute into the standardization formula:
$$\frac{7.7 - \mu}{\sigma} = -0.935$$
Multiply both sides by $\sigma$ and rearrange:
$$7.7 - \mu = -0.935\sigma \implies \mu - 0.935\sigma = 7.7 \quad \text{[Equation 2]}$$

Eliminate $\mu$ by subtracting Equation 2 from Equation 1:
$$(\mu + 0.674\sigma) - (\mu - 0.935\sigma) = 8.8 - 7.7$$
$$(0.674 + 0.935)\sigma = 1.1$$
$$1.609\sigma = 1.1$$
Divide both sides by $1.609$:
$$\sigma = \frac{1.1}{1.609} \approx 0.68365 \approx 0.684$$

Substitute $\sigma = 0.68365$ into Equation 1 to find $\mu$:
$$\mu = 8.8 - 0.674 \times 0.68365 = 8.8 - 0.46078 = 8.3392 \approx 8.34$$
Verify using Equation 2:
$$\mu = 7.7 + 0.935 \times 0.68365 = 7.7 + 0.63921 = 8.3392 \approx 8.34$$
The parameters are $\mu = 8.34$ and $\sigma = 0.684$.

hints: Find the probability $p$ that a single randomly selected woman has a middle finger shorter than 8.2 cm using normal standardization $Z = \dfrac{X - \mu}{\sigma}$.
Look up $\Phi(z)$ in the normal distribution tables to obtain the value of $p$.
Model the number of women out of 5 with fingers shorter than 8.2 cm as a binomial variable $W \sim \mathrm{B}(5, p)$ and calculate $\mathrm{P}(W = 3) = \binom{5}{3} p^3 (1-p)^2$.
walkthrough:
Standardize to find the probability that a single woman has a middle finger shorter than $8.2$ cm:
$$X \sim \mathrm{N}(7.9, 0.44^2)$$
$$Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma} = \frac{8.2 - 7.9}{0.44} = \frac{0.3}{0.44} = \frac{15}{22} \approx 0.6818$$

Find the cumulative probability from standard normal tables:
$$p = \mathrm{P}(X < 8.2) = \Phi(0.6818) \approx 0.7524$$

Define the binomial random variable $W$, the number of women out of $5$ with finger length shorter than $8.2$ cm:
$$W \sim \mathrm{B}(5, p) \quad \text{where } p = 0.7524, \; 1 - p = 0.2476$$

Calculate the binomial probability for $W = 3$:
$$\mathrm{P}(W = 3) = \binom{5}{3} p^3 (1 - p)^2 = \binom{5}{3} (0.7524)^3 (0.2476)^2$$
$$\mathrm{P}(W = 3) = 10 \times 0.42594 \times 0.061306 \approx 0.2611 \approx 0.261$$
teacher_walkthrough: Recognize this as a two-stage probability problem: first find the probability $p$ for an individual woman using the normal distribution, then find the probability for a sample of $5$ women using the binomial distribution.

For one woman, finger length $X$ follows $\mathrm{N}(7.9, 0.44^2)$. Standardize $X = 8.2$:
$$Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma} = \frac{8.2 - 7.9}{0.44} = \frac{0.30}{0.44} \approx 0.6818$$
Look up $z = 0.6818$ in the normal distribution tables:
$$\Phi(0.68) = 0.7517, \quad \text{difference for } 2 \text{ is } 7 \implies \Phi(0.682) = 0.7524$$
Thus, the probability of success for an individual is $p = 0.7524$, and the probability of failure is:
$$q = 1 - p = 1 - 0.7524 = 0.2476$$

Let $W$ denote the number of women in the sample of $n = 5$ with finger length shorter than $8.2$ cm.
$W$ follows a binomial distribution $W \sim \mathrm{B}(5, 0.7524)$. Write the binomial probability formula:
$$\mathrm{P}(W = r) = \binom{n}{r} p^r (1 - p)^{n - r}$$

hints: Write the standardization equation $Z = \dfrac{X - \mu}{\sigma}$ for the boundary value $1.5\mu$.
Substitute the given condition $\sigma = \mu$ into the expression so that $\mu$ cancels, then look up $\Phi(z)$ in the normal distribution table.
walkthrough:
Write down the standardization formula for $X < 1.5\mu$:
$$Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma} = \frac{1.5\mu - \mu}{\sigma}$$

Use the given condition that the mean equals the standard deviation ($\sigma = \mu$) to simplify the fraction:
$$Z = \frac{1.5\mu - \mu}{\mu} = \frac{0.5\mu}{\mu} = 0.5$$

Find the cumulative probability from the standard normal tables:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 1.5\mu) = \mathrm{P}(Z < 0.5) = \Phi(0.5) = 0.6915 \approx 0.692$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Start with the standard normal transformation:
$$Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma}$$
We want to evaluate $\mathrm{P}(X < 1.5\mu)$.

Substitute the upper limit $X = 1.5\mu$ and replace $\sigma$ with $\mu$ since the problem states that the mean equals the standard deviation ($\sigma = \mu$):
$$Z = \frac{1.5\mu - \mu}{\mu}$$
Factor out $\mu$ in the numerator:
$$1.5\mu - \mu = (1.5 - 1)\mu = 0.5\mu$$
Cancel $\mu$ from numerator and denominator:
$$Z = \frac{0.5\mu}{\mu} = 0.5$$
The unknown parameter $\mu$ cancels out completely, leaving an exact $z$-value of $0.5$.

Look up $z = 0.5$ in the standard normal distribution table:
$$\Phi(0.50) = 0.6915$$
Round to $3$ significant figures:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 1.5\mu) = 0.6915 \approx 0.692$$
